title: An affine nonzero section gives vanishing of ideal twists on a proper integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $n\ge1$ be an integer and let $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})$ be a nonzero global section whose nonvanishing open $C_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is affine. For every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_C$ [pqf-def-coherent], there exists an integer $E\ge1$ such that $H^1(C,\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal N^{\otimes En})=0$. Cohomology is as in [pqf-def-cohomology], and tensor products and powers are as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, third paragraph beginning We will show: injective ideal-twist maps, zero-dimensional cokernels, surjections on H1 and finite-basis annihilation (varieties.tex lines 10038-10066).

proof.text: Put $L=\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$ and $F_e=\mathcal I\otimes L^{\otimes e}$ for $e\ge0$, with $F_0=\mathcal I$. By [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent], $C$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal O_C$ is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2), the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_C$ is coherent. In a local trivialization of $\mathcal N$, every $F_e$ identifies with $\mathcal I$, so it is coherent. The same trivializations show that $L$ and its powers are invertible. Also $C$ is quasi-compact, being Noetherian, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], since it is locally Noetherian.

proof.text:
On a nonempty affine trivializing open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the section $s$ has a coefficient $a\in A$, and $A$ is a domain. This coefficient is nonzero: if $s$ vanished on $V$, any other nonempty affine trivializing open $W$ would meet $V$ by irreducibility; choose a nonempty basic open $D(f)\subseteq W\cap V$. Its coefficient $b$ would have $b/1=0$ in the localization at $f
e0$, forcing $b=0$ in the domain. Such $W$ cover $C$, contradicting $s
e0$. Thus $a
e0$ on every $V$. On $V$, the map $u_e:F_e	o F_{e+1}$ given by tensoring with $s$ is multiplication by $a$ on the ideal $\mathcal I(V)\subseteq A$, which is injective since $A$ is a domain; it is an isomorphism on $D(a)$. These local calculations prove that $u_e$ is injective everywhere and an isomorphism over $C_s$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, third paragraph beginning We will show: injective ideal-twist maps, zero-dimensional cokernels, surjections on H1 and finite-basis annihilation (varieties.tex lines 10038-10066).

proof.text: Let $Q_e=\operatorname{Coker}(u_e)$. It is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1), and its support is contained in the closed subset $Z=C\setminus C_s$. The subset $Z$ is proper: on any nonempty affine trivializing open the nonzero coefficient $a$ has the generic prime $(0)$ in $D(a)$, so $C_s\ne\varnothing$. To check the dimension bound even without assuming the support closed, take any strict chain $Y_0\subsetneq Y_1$ of nonempty irreducible relatively closed subsets of $\operatorname{Supp}(Q_e)$. Their closures in $C$ are irreducible closed subsets contained in $Z$; they remain distinct because intersecting each closure with $\operatorname{Supp}(Q_e)$ recovers $Y_i$. Appending $C$ gives a chain of length two in the irreducible space $C$, contradicting $\dim C=1$. Thus $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(Q_e)\le0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, third paragraph beginning We will show: injective ideal-twist maps, zero-dimensional cokernels, surjections on H1 and finite-basis annihilation (varieties.tex lines 10038-10066).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-coherent-zero-dimensional-support] to each $Q_e$ on the locally Noetherian scheme $C$ to obtain $H^1(C,Q_e)=0$. The short exact sequence $0\to F_e\xrightarrow{u_e}F_{e+1}\to Q_e\to0$ gives, by [pqf-def-cohomology], the exact segment $H^1(C,F_e)\to H^1(C,F_{e+1})\to H^1(C,Q_e)$. Thus every transition $H^1(u_e)$ is surjective, and their composite $T_e:H^1(C,\mathcal I)\to H^1(C,F_e)$ is surjective as well. These are $k$-linear maps, obtained by applying the derived global-section functor to $\mathcal O_C$-linear maps. The cohomology in the vanishing node is the same right-derived module global sections as in [pqf-def-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, third paragraph beginning We will show: injective ideal-twist maps, zero-dimensional cokernels, surjections on H1 and finite-basis annihilation (varieties.tex lines 10038-10066).

proof.text: For every $\xi\in H^1(C,\mathcal I)$ apply [lem-sc-section-affine-open-kills-cohomology] with $X=C$, the invertible module $L=\mathcal N^{\otimes n}$, the given $s$, $F=\mathcal I$, and $p=1$. The scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 1, $C_s$ is affine by hypothesis, and $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent. We obtain $e(\xi)\ge0$ with $T_{e(\xi)}(\xi)=0$: the composite $u_{e-1}\cdots u_0$ is precisely tensoring with $s^{\otimes e}$, as is checked in each trivialization by multiplication by $a^e$.

source.place: Tag 0B5X, lemma-ample-curve, proof, third paragraph beginning We will show: injective ideal-twist maps, zero-dimensional cokernels, surjections on H1 and finite-basis annihilation (varieties.tex lines 10038-10066).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-coherent-hi] applied to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the coherent ideal $\mathcal I$, the vector space $V=H^1(C,\mathcal I)$ is finite-dimensional; a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Choose a finite basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$. Choose annihilating exponents $e_i$ as in step 5 and put $E=\max(1,e_1,\ldots,e_r)$, taking $E=1$ if $r=0$. For each $i$, functoriality factors $T_E$ through $T_{e_i}$, so $T_E(v_i)=0$. Every vector is a linear combination of the $v_i$, hence $T_E=0$. Since $T_E$ is surjective by step 4, its target $H^1(C,F_E)$ is zero. Finally $F_E\cong\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes En}$ by grouping the tensor factors, which gives the assertion with $E\ge1$.
